hook.line: Let's talk about how I got these results on Pinterest.
hook.visual: Woman cut out over a Pinterest Analytics screenshot (impressions +205%, saves +450%), with the title 'How I Grew My Pinterest Account' across her chest.

beats.what: 30-day analytics screenshot behind her with green growth percentages, title text over her
Small sentence captions replace the title: brand-new account, only fresh content
Explains posting 3-6 fresh pins a day while gesturing with her hands
Keyword-optimised profile, pin titles and boards
Cut: background becomes a 90-day impressions graph; she shrinks to the bottom-left corner
She points up at the curve where it starts to climb in September
Payoff: growth takes three to six months, as the graph shows
Asks for questions in the comments and a follow, over the graph

why_it_works: Real analytics with big green percentages sit behind her from frame one, so the proof is on screen before the first sentence ends
She saves the honest part ('what people won't show you': the flat first month) for the second half and shows it as a graph, which rewards viewers who stayed
Shrinking herself into the corner at the cut hands the frame to the chart, so the one layout change marks the payoff
Ends on a question prompt, which invites comments from people with their own Pinterest problems
weaknesses: 55 s before the first cut with a static screenshot; the middle tips run long
Captions are small (about 2.6% of frame height) and sit over busy UI text
Fast talking (3.75 words/s) with dense tips; hard to retain without saving
for_robert: Hold one layout for the tips, then make a single big layout change for the proof: Robert shrinks to a corner and Fred points at the graph's turning point.
